_comment: The browse acceptance suite. Each task is run through the REAL `browse` tool
against the REAL web with the REAL providers, and scored by a GROUNDED check
— never by asking a model whether the answer looks good.
`check` kinds, all evaluated in code by scripts/browse_bench.py:
records_at_least  — the run gathered >= n structured records
field_present     — every gathered record carries this field
price_grounded    — the cheapest/most expensive price named in the answer
actually appears in the gathered records
url_contains      — the final page's URL contains this substring
text_contains_any — the final page's text contains one of these strings
Tasks are deliberately ordinary — the ones a user actually asked for on
2026-07-26 and all four of which failed. A benchmark of things we already

tasks.why: THE INCIDENT TASK. Failed live 2026-07-26: three empty extracts, then 'the page didn't respond'.
tasks.goal: Search for Yonex badminton rackets and extract the top 5 products with their names and prices

tasks.why: A stable, scraping-friendly control. If this fails the harness itself is broken, not the site.
tasks.goal: Extract the names and prices of the books listed on this page

tasks.why: Multi-step: the loop must ACT (open a category) and then read, not just read the landing page.
tasks.goal: Open the Travel category and extract the names and prices of the books in it

tasks.why: Gather ACROSS pages — working memory has to carry records past a navigation.
tasks.goal: Extract the quotes and their authors from the first two pages of this site

tasks.why: Failed live 2026-07-26 (hit the action cap after a real extract). A commercial site with heavy JS.
tasks.goal: Search for wireless earbuds and extract the first 5 listings with their prices

tasks.why: A prose page: the structural reader must DECLINE and the LLM path must carry it.
tasks.goal: Find out what year the Eiffel Tower was completed
